course_title: Research in musculoskeletal, sports and exercise physiotherapy
course_description:
Advances student's understanding of and capacity to undertake research in musculoskeletal and sports and exercise physiotherapy.

In PHTY7954 students advance their understanding of research and its application to sports and musculoskeletal physiotherapy practice. Students will develop an understanding of different types of research and how best to translate that research into their practice. Students will also gain first-hand experience in critical analysis of literature, and research processes including data collection, data-analysis, interpretation of data and the writing of a case report.

course_aims: To develop students understanding of research, ability to critique literature and capacity to undertake a research project relevant to the physiotherapy profession.

learning_outcomes.description: Understand key research methodologies in physiotherapy and health literature.
Interpret and apply research findings to inform clinical practice.
Understand the role of consumers and the public in research design and translation.
Recognise the benefits of quality improvement projects in health services.
Evaluate research quality using contemporary methodological frameworks.
Conduct a research project demonstrating effective project management and data analysis.
Create an original research manuscript suitable for scientific publication.

assessment_details.title: Critical Appraisal Assignment
assessment_details.task_description: Students will critically appraise a clinical trial research article of their choice and submit their appraisal as a written assignment. Students will be guided in the use of PEDRO as the tool for the assignment, since it is designed specifically to critically appraise physiotherapy trials. The Webcast provided in Week 2 will also provide guidance for the completion of this critical appraisal. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance. assessment_details.title: Case Report
assessment_details.task_description: Each student will conduct a formal Case Report during the semester using a patient in their current caseload. The Case Report will follow a formal structure including relevant literature review, formulation of a research question, collection of appropriate outcome measures, analysis of the measures, and interpretation of findings. This will be presented as a written Case Report formatted for a journal submission. Article length must be 2000 words or less. The Case Report will be written according to JOSPT Cases Instructions to Authors and the CARE guidelines as are provided to students: - JOSPT Cases Instructions to Authors - CARE Case Report Guidelines (https://www.care-statement.org/) - CARE Checklist — CARE Case Report Guidelines (https://www.care-statement.org/checklist) Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 10 (27 Jul - 11 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Webcasts regarding research design and translation to practice Students will watch a series of webcasts describing different research methodologies (e.g., quantitative, qualitative, clinical trials, etc) with the intent of better informing their interpretation and application of research literature to practice. Students will be assessed on their learning/knowledge from the webcasts. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13 (27 Jul - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Experience in conducting research Students will gain experience in conducting research through the undertaking of a Case Report using a patient in their current clinical caseload. In preparation students will watch a specific webcast in Week 1 of Semester with associated readings which will permit them to use appropriate frameworks to develop the Case Report. This formal structure will include a relevant literature review, formulation of a research question, collection of appropriate outcome measures, analysis of the measures, and interpretation of findings. Students will present this as a written Case Report in a format appropriate for journal submission. Learning outcomes: L02, L04, L06, L07

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 2 To Week 8 (03 Aug - 20 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Development of research critical appraisal skills Critical appraisal skills are vital for clinicians to systematically evaluate the trustworthiness, relevance, and results of published literature. In this component of the course, students will watch a specific webcast with associated readings which will permit them to use appropriate frameworks to critically appraise research articles. They will be assessed on this learning activity. Learning outcomes: L03, L04, L05
